Subject: Data purge request: test environment prompts & logs

Hi Soojin,

We need Redwood's assistance to fully purge prompt inputs, assistant outputs, and request/response logs associated with our 'sandbox' and 'staging' projects (project IDs: FT-SBX-21, FT-STG-09). This is a compliance-driven request: we must provide a signed confirmation and evidence for our auditors (SOC2 scope).

Questions we have up front:
- Do your KV cache snapshots and prefix caches get scrubbed as part of a purge, or are those handled separately?
- What artifacts will you provide as proof (audit CSV with record ids, ops ticket PDF, cryptographic digests, S3 object deletion manifests, etc.)?
- Timeline: can you complete the purge and provide proof within 48 hours once we approve the action?
- Do you retain any aggregated telemetry derived from these requests that could be considered re-identifiable?

Please advise the required approvals we need to route, and whether you need any additional account or dataset identifiers.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Platform Ops, FinnoTech
ops@finnotech.com

Subject: Re: Data purge request: test environment prompts & logs

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear request. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (security/ops) to confirm the technical workflow and evidence package.

High-level answers:
- KV/prefix caches: those are part of the purge for sandbox/staging when requested; we will include cache invalidation and zeroization steps in the runbook.
- Proof artifacts: we produce an ops ticket PDF (ticket id), a scrub_audit CSV listing object keys and timestamps, and S3 deletion manifests where applicable. We can also provide SHA-256 digests of deleted blobs as an additional handback artifact.
- Timeline: target 48 hours SLA is achievable for sandbox/staging, provided you confirm the project IDs and approve the action. If there are cross-region snapshots we may need up to 72 hours.
- Aggregated telemetry: we keep aggregate service metrics (latency, counts) but do not keep request/response content after purge. We will explicitly state what we retain in the confirmation.

Action items for FinnoTech to approve:
1) Confirm FT-SBX-21 and FT-STG-09 are the only projects to purge.
2) Approve the purge window (we propose start: 2027-12-05 09:00 PST).
3) Confirm if you need cryptographic digests included in the evidence bundle.

Ben will prepare the technical runbook and RFC; Marissa will coordinate the final confirmation email back to your audit team.

Best,
So: Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Data purge request: test environment prompts & logs — technical runbook

Hi all,

Outlined below is the technical purge workflow (summary) that Ops will execute once FinnoTech approves. I included where we will collect proof. This will be committed as an ops ticket and signed off by our security lead.

Scope: projects FT-SBX-21, FT-STG-09 (sandbox, staging).

Steps:
1) Snapshot current state (read-only export): list of object keys from request logs (S3), query ids from request db (Postgres), KV cache keys (in-memory/redis snapshots). Timestamped snapshot stored to an encrypted, short-lived bucket for audit and then deleted after proof generation.
2) Invalidate runtime caches: remove prefix caches and evict KV cache shards for the two projects.
3) Delete objects: issue S3 DeleteObjects calls for identified keys (multi-part where required). For request logs stored in Postgres, we will run parameterized DELETE where project_id IN (FT-SBX-21, FT-STG-09) (we will capture row counts and query ids).
4) Rotate keys used for any secondary stores that may have embedded artifacts (if applicable).
5) Proof generation:
   - scrub_audit_20271204.csv: row per deleted artifact with columns: store,type,object_key,deleted_at,deleted_by,sha256_digest
   - ops_ticket_12345.pdf: ticket with execution timeline and approver signature (ops).
   - s3_delete_manifest.json (human-readable) for internal use.
6) Independent verification: our security team will run a read-only verification script to attempt retrieval of deleted keys; verification results will be included in the evidence bundle.

Notes/answers to Elena's questions:
- KV/prefix cache handling: we will both evict caches and perform zeroization of persisted cache snapshots. If you have a separate customer-managed cache (outside Redwood runtime), note that remains in your environment.
- Aggregated telemetry: we will include the list of telemetry categories we retain (counts by model/route) in the confirmation; no content-level telemetry is kept once purge completes.

Risks/edge cases:
- Cross-region replication delays: if any of your objects were replicated to another region before purge, we will include those replicated object keys in the runbook and purge them; coordination may add ~24 hours.
- Long-tail backups: daily backups older than 30 days are immutable in backup vaults; our policy is to note their existence in the evidence and mark a retention exception if applicable.

Estimated time: 36–48 hours for scoped projects, 72 hours if replication/backups included.

Attachments: ops_ticket_12345.pdf (will be created when ticket is opened).

Ben Carter
Security & Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

This is Marissa from Redwood Customer Success. Per the approved runbook (Ops Ticket ID: OT-12345), the purge for FT-SBX-21 and FT-STG-09 was executed on 2027-12-05 starting at 09:05 PST and completed on 2027-12-05 at 20:22 PST. Below is the human-readable summary; the full evidence bundle is attached.

Summary (high level):

Artifacts attached:

- scrub_audit_20271204.csv (CSV: store,type,object_key,deleted_at,deleted_by,sha256_digest)
